questions.text: How is the constructor property different from the [[Prototype]] link?
options: constructor is an ordinary property, usually stored on prototype. [[Prototype]] is the internal link that lookup walks
They are two names for the same pointer
[[Prototype]] stores the function name, constructor stores the chain
constructor changes instanceof, and [[Prototype]] does not affect it

questions.text: What does assignment do when the chain finds a setter?
options: It creates an own property and ignores the setter
It calls the setter. No own property with that name is created
It rewrites the setter on the prototype
It deletes the setter and writes the value onto the prototype

questions.text: Why does for...in not show class methods?
options: for...in cannot read prototype
Class methods live on the instance but are hidden from the loop
Class methods are non-enumerable
The loop sees only static methods

questions.text: Where does a class field n = 1 get stored?
options: On the constructor’s prototype
On the constructor function itself
In the closure of the module that declared the class
On the instance, as an own property

questions.text: A parent field initializer creates an own property on the child instance.
Assignment to an inherited writable property changes the value on the prototype itself.
The in operator finds a non-enumerable class method that lives on the prototype.
Object.setPrototypeOf changes the prototype of an existing object, and later reads follow the new chain.
Which object does the search in super.n() start from?
questions.answer: From the [[Prototype]] of the method’s home object, not from this.

questions.text: How do you read exactly one link of the prototype chain?
What from an object reaches JSON.stringify when some names are visible only through the prototype?
questions.answer: Only own enumerable properties. Inherited fields are left out of the string.

questions.text: What is the [[Prototype]] of an ordinary function function f() {}?
What does Object.assign copy?
options: Own enumerable properties. It copies neither the prototype link nor inherited keys
The whole prototype chain, keys included
Only the [[Prototype]] link
Every own property, including non-enumerable ones

questions.text: How far does proto.isPrototypeOf(obj) look?
options: It compares proto with obj.constructor
Along the whole prototype chain of obj, not only at the direct prototype
It checks only Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)
It looks at the class name as a string

questions.text: Why does constructor point at Object after Box.prototype = { n: 1 } for a new object?
options: new always installs Object
Assigning prototype erases the function Box
The new prototype object has no own constructor, so the read reaches Object.prototype
constructor is taken from the first argument of new

questions.text: Where does a static method live, and how does a subclass find it?
options: On prototype, next to instance methods
The subclass copies statics onto itself as own properties
The instance inherits statics through its own chain
On the constructor function. The subclass finds it through its own [[Prototype]]: class B extends A links B to A

questions.text: Instances created before Box.prototype is replaced keep the previous prototype object.
An object in the middle of the chain can hide a property of a prototype further up.
Array.prototype.map.call can run map with an array-like object as this.
Reading a key that exists nowhere in the chain throws a ReferenceError.
Which object is the direct prototype of an array?
What does an array-like object need for a method such as map to work through call?
questions.answer: A length number and indexed elements. map reads them from this.

questions.text: How does a shared method see one instance’s data?
questions.answer: Through this. A call with a dot supplies the instance, and its fields live on that instance.

questions.text: What does delete obj.missing return when that key exists neither on the object nor in the chain?
questions.answer: true. There was nothing to delete, and for an ordinary object that is not an error.

questions.text:
console.log(Array.prototype.isPrototypeOf([]) ? 1 : 0);
console.log(Function.prototype.isPrototypeOf(Array) ? 1 : 0);
What happens in strict mode when you assign to an inherited property with writable: false?
options: A TypeError. No own property is created, and the prototype value stays
An own property is created on top
The value on the prototype changes
The key is removed from the chain

questions.text: Which two links does class B extends A create?
options: Only a B instance gets an A instance as its prototype
B.prototype’s [[Prototype]] becomes A.prototype, and the function B’s [[Prototype]] becomes A
B.prototype becomes A, with no separate link between the functions
Both functions share one prototype object

questions.text: Does delete obj.n remove the property from the prototype when obj has no own n?
options: Yes, the key disappears for everyone who shares that prototype
Yes, but only when the property is enumerable
No. delete affects only an own property. When there is none, the call returns true and the prototype stays
The call throws a TypeError

questions.text: Where does a getter on the prototype get this?
options: From the object where the getter was declared
From the global object
A getter’s this is always undefined
From the object it was read through

questions.text: A method added with Object.assign(Ctor.prototype, mixin) is visible to instances created earlier too.
Properties from the second argument of Object.create(proto, descriptors) become own properties.
For a constructor declared with function, the prototype of the Box.prototype object is Object.prototype.
The function Array has Function.prototype in its chain, so Array instanceof Function.
Why does replacing a method on the same prototype object show up on old instances, while replacing Box.prototype does not?
questions.answer: Old instances keep a link to the previous prototype object. A new property is looked up on the object already in their chain. Only later new calls receive the new Box.prototype.

questions.text: What does object spread do with a method the instance only inherits?
questions.answer: It does not copy it. Spread takes own enumerable properties, and a method on the prototype is not one of them.

questions.text: How is the Box.prototype property different from the [[Prototype]] of the function Box?
questions.answer: Box.prototype is an ordinary property. new uses it as the instance’s prototype. [[Prototype]] is the function’s own internal link, not the prototype property.

questions.text: What does a child instance see when the child overrides a method and does not call super?
questions.answer: The child method. The parent method of the same name is no longer found from that instance.
